newsitem.title: USA: Viacom stock jumps on share buyback plan.
newsitem.headline: Viacom stock jumps on share buyback plan.

text.p: Viacom Inc's share price jumped on news of a plan by the company and its top shareholder to buy back as much as six percent of Viacom's depressed stock.
The $500 million buyback comes just before a key meeting with analysts and marks the end of the entertainment giant's long restriction on repurchases.

Early Thursday Viacom said it, its chairman Sumner Redstone and his National Amusements Inc intended to buy up to $500 million in Viacom shares and warrants -- $250 million by Viacom and up to $250 million by National and/or Redstone.

"It is a statement by the company that they consider the shares very undervalued," said Edward Hatch of UBS Securities. "The buyback is split between a personal purchase by Redstone through National Amusements and Viacom itself."
Viacom's Class A shares were up almost eight percent, or 2-3/8, to 32-3/4 on the American Stock Exchange, while the non-voting Class B shares added 2-1/4 to 33-1/8, also on the AMEX.
The "A" shares have tumbled from a high of about 54 last September. The "B" shares have largely mirrored the descent.
The buyback's timing "comes after the first clearance they have had after the spinoff of the cable systems," Hatch said. "Share repurchases were restricted for some time because of that."
Viacom's complex spin-off of its cable operations to Tele-Communications Inc, valued at $2.3 billion, closed on July 31, a Viacom spokesman said.
"The company was not permitted to purchase shares while the deal was pending for over a year, and also was not able to do so immediately after" the deal closed, a source close to Viacom said.
The buyback announcement was made after a "comfort level" was reached regarding the end of restriction, as opposed to a specific "green light" date, the source said.
Hatch said that "based on the public float, it is a meaningful buyback of about six percent of outstanding shares across both classes, excluding what is owned by Redstone already."
National Amusements and Viacom will finance the repurchases from their working capital, they said.

"We consider the shares cheap and the share repurchase probably marks the first catalyst to increase investor interest, especially since there is a major analyst meeting October 8, with all the division heads to be there," Hatch added.
He said UBS rates the stock a buy, with a six- to 12-month price target of $45 per share.

National Amusements acquired control of Viacom in June 1987 and owns about 65 percent of Viacom's Class A shares and about 26 percent of the Class A and Class B common on a combined basis, according to Viacom.

National Amusements, closely-held and controlled by Redstone, completed a stock purchase program in August 1993 under which it acquired 1.47 million Viacom Class A shares and 1.9 million Class B shares.
The Viacom spokesman said that as of June 30 there were 69.9 million Class A shares and 286.7 million Class B shares outstanding.
